pool.text: The Creek were forced to leave the area under Indian Removal.
The residents approved, and the town was incorporated as Atlanta.
Confederate General John Bell Hood decided to retreat from Atlanta.
The state capital was moved from Milledgeville to Atlanta.
The founding of the Georgia School of Technology and Atlanta University Center.
Atlanta hosted the Cotton States and International Exposition.
Atlanta hosted the film premiere of Gone with the Wind.
The mayor ordered the hiring of the first African-American police officers.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution formed resulting from a major merger between two local newspapers.
African Americans elected Atlanta's first Black mayor, Maynard Jackson.
The opening of the Georgia World Congress Center confirmed Atlanta's convention rise.
Rail service commenced for the city's newly built subway system.
Staff consolidation occurred for The Atlanta Journal and The Atlanta Constitution newspapers.
Trees Atlanta was founded as a non-profit organization in the city.
Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport became the world's busiest airport by traffic.
Shirley Franklin became the first woman to be elected mayor.
Separate publication of the morning Constitution and afternoon Journal newspapers officially ceased.
The city approved the multi-billion dollar Beltline project.
Mayor Bill Campbell was convicted by a federal jury on tax evasion.
The Beltline project received a federal grant of $18 million.
